messages.text: Verstappen, Lawson receive grid penalties after 'unacceptable' practice collision

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both received one-grid place penalties for an "unacceptable" collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Max Verstappen, Liam Lawson receive grid penalties for 'unacceptable' practice collision at Mexico City Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Max Verstappen, Liam Lawson receive grid penalties for 'unacceptable' practice collision at Mexico City Grand Prix Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both been handed a one-place grid penalty for their collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix; watch qualifying in Mexico at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 31 October 2026 07:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson have both received one-grid place penalties for an "unacceptable" collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Verstappen tried to overtake Lawson up the inside at Turn 12 going into the old baseball stadium but the Racing Bulls driver held his ground, so the pair went side by side through Turn 13 and made contact at Turn 14 with a piece of debris falling off the Dutchman's car and causing a red flag. Collisions of this nature between drivers in practice are extremely rare, and the stewards stated both drivers "behaved in a manner that was considered unacceptable" and that a warning had been given at the team managers' meeting earlier on Friday about overtaking in the final sector. messages.text: Arbeloa: We've made mistakes but Fulham on right path

metadata.summary: Having gone winless in your first six games and conceded goals at a rate of almost two a game, there are worse ways to recover than a pair of gritty 1-0 victories.
metadata.content: Alvaro Arbeloa exclusive: Fulham head coach on early mistakes, seeing out games and getting the best from Gonzalo Garcia | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Alvaro Arbeloa exclusive: Fulham head coach on early mistakes, seeing out games and getting the best from Gonzalo Garcia Alvaro Arbeloa on Fulham's difficult start, changing his system and why Gonzalo Garcia will come good; Watch Aston Villa vs Fulham live on Sky Sports Premier League from 8pm on Saturday, kick-off 7.45pm Ron Walker Football Journalist @Ronnabe Saturday 31 October 2026 10:18, UK Image: Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham face Aston Villa on Saturday night Having gone winless in your first six games and conceded goals at a rate of almost two a game, there are worse ways to recover than a pair of gritty 1-0 victories. It is still early days in the Alvaro Arbeloa project at Fulham but the optimism a narrow but entertaining opening-weekend 3-2 defeat to Chelsea had brought from his debut in the dugout had quickly waned with such a poor run which had left them stranded bottom of the Premier League. That openness which initially seemed a welcome tonic from the sometimes pragmatic Marco Silva era had quickly become the problem, with the Cottagers losing 3-2 again - this time to previously winless Crystal Palace - and shipping two late goals to Ipswich earlier this month to lose at Portman Road too. messages.text: Leclerc seals Mexico City practice double as Hamilton suffers technical issue

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue.
metadata.content: Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc completes Friday practice double as Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc completes Friday practice double as Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure Charles Leclerc tops both Friday practice sessions for Ferrari; Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure; Max Verstappen collides with Liam Lawson; watch every Mexico City GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 31 October 2026 03:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Mexico City Grand Prix Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue. Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers. Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth.
